html:
SMTO-UI-0004 — This file is too big to attach

GUID: efbd19fb-8f6b-4336-b6f8-04377af1dc82
Slug: ui-attachment-too-large
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The file is bigger than SMTO allows for one attachment (64 MB unless your administrator changed it). It wasn't added, and files you already attached are unaffected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make the file smaller: compress it, save it in a smaller format, or split it into several files. Each file must be under the size limit on its own.
  2. Attach the smaller file, or each part, to your message. Files under the limit are accepted normally.
  3. If you regularly need bigger files, ask your administrator to raise Maximum attachment size (bytes) in Settings › Operate › Execution. The limit is a server setting that only an administrator can change.

What success looks like

  • The file appears among your message's attachments without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the file's size. Don't delete earlier attachments or conversations to make room; this limit is about the size of each file, not your total storage.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An attachment was refused because the file exceeds the per-file limit (attachment_max_file_bytes, default 64 MiB), checked in the browser against /api/agent/context/limits and enforced by the upload stage with HTTP 413.

What this means

  • Browser or server attachment validation rejects content larger than 64 MiB. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Browser or server attachment validation rejects content larger than 64 MiB.

How to diagnose it

  • Check byte length against the per-file limit before selecting the attachment again.

How to fix it

  • Reduce or split the file below the limit reported by GET /api/agent/context/limits. An administrator can change the limit in Settings › Operate › Execution › Maximum attachment size (bytes); new uploads use the new value, stored attachments stay available, and analysis tools keep their own limits.
  • Reduce or split the attachment to fit the displayed upload limit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Each intended attachment is within 64 MiB and accepted through normal context ownership checks.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
